title: EBP field-script data - treasure chests (setuptreasure records) and traps

container.notes: Records live in the data block of the compiled field script (EBP section 0) of each map, e.g. ald_a01.ebp. The ff12-script decompiler writes that script as <map>.c (code) plus <map>.src.data (data arrays); the chest table and the trap table are arrays in the data file, used by the script functions setuptreasure / trap setup. No magic or header: chest records are a contiguous run of 24-byte records ordered by chestIndex. Locate them with the per-record offsets of the Vanilla Chests sheet or by scanning for runs of records whose first byte counts 0,1,2... with three zero bytes after it. Little-endian.

records.name: treasureChest
records.count: one per chest of the map (1-11 per map in the samples; 1966 records in the whole game per the sheet)
records.where: Data block of the map's compiled field script (EBP section 0; `<map>.src.data` after decompiling with ff12-script). Records are contiguous with a 24-byte stride, ordered by chestIndex; record k = table start + 24*k. The Vanilla Chests sheet gives every record's hex offset (column F), e.g. ald_a01 0x40, 0x58, 0x70 ...; bds_a01 from 0x240.

fields.name: chestIndex
fields.notes: Per-map chest index (0..n-1); bit number of the map's opened-chest flag. Do not renumber.

fields.name: unused01
fields.notes: Always 00 00 00 in the sampled rows; keep as read.

fields.name: posX
fields.notes: Signed 16-bit position, first axis (sheet "X").

fields.name: posY
fields.notes: Signed 16-bit position, second axis (sheet "Y"; probably world Z).

fields.name: flags

bits.name: unknownBits0to5
bits.notes: Unknown; multiples of 5 rising with the chest index in the samples. Keep.

fields.notes: Bit 6 = randomize gil. Bits 0-5 and 7 unknown (keep).

fields.name: uniqueSpawnId
fields.notes: 255 = normal (respawning) chest; other values = id of a once-only chest shared by all records with the same id.

fields.name: spawnChance
fields.notes: Spawn chance in percent.

fields.name: gilChance
fields.notes: Percent chance that the chest holds gil instead of an item.

fields.name: itemLow
fields.notes: Content id; 50% pick without Diamond Armlet ("Low Item").

fields.name: itemHigh
fields.notes: Content id; 50% pick without Diamond Armlet ("High Item").

fields.name: itemDiamondCommon
fields.notes: Content id; 95% pick with Diamond Armlet.

fields.name: itemDiamondRare
fields.notes: Content id; 5% pick with Diamond Armlet.

fields.name: gil
fields.notes: Gil amount (plain number).

fields.name: gilDiamond
fields.notes: Gil amount with Diamond Armlet (equal to gil in the samples).

records.name: trapTableHeader
records.where: Trap table in the same script data block, e.g. srb_b04.src.data offset 0x390 (count 5).

fields.name: trapCount
fields.notes: Number of traps; trapCount u32 offsets follow, relative to this field.

records.name: trapOffset
records.where: Directly after trapCount: entry i at trapCount address + 4 + 4*i.

fields.name: offset
fields.notes: Offset of trap i relative to the trapCount field.

records.name: trap
records.where: At trapCount address + trapOffset[i].offset (first trap of srb_b04 at 0x3AC).

fields.name: posX
fields.notes: Trap position X (s16 assumed; described as ushort).

fields.name: posZ
fields.notes: Trap position Z.

fields.name: uniqueFlagIndex
fields.notes: 0xFF = always respawns; other values index the non-respawn flag array (once-only).

fields.name: unknown05
fields.notes: 0x64 or 0 observed; meaning unknown (spawn chance?).

fields.name: action1
fields.notes: Trap action A (one of the two is picked at random).

fields.name: action2
fields.notes: Trap action B.

fields.name: unknown0A
fields.notes: Always 0x0A observed; unknown.

roundTrip: Edit fields in place only: the record size (24 bytes, 12 for traps) and the number of records are fixed by the compiled script; never insert, delete or reorder records in a .src.data block.
Keep chestIndex unchanged: it is the per-map bit number of the opened-chest flag, so renumbering would swap the saved opened state between chests and can collide with other chests of the map.
Copy unused01 (+0x01..+0x03) and flags bits 0-5 and 7 back exactly as read.
uniqueSpawnId: keep 255 for respawning chests. A value other than 255 links the chest to every other chest with the same id (only one of them can ever be looted); reuse an id only on purpose.
Item fields (+0x0C..+0x12) are content ids (category << 12 | index, see enums-content-ids); gil fields (+0x14, +0x16) are plain unsigned amounts, not content ids.
Positions are signed 16-bit values; write them back with the same sign convention.
spawnChance and gilChance are percentages; keep them in 0-100.
Trap offsets are relative to the trapCount field; editing trap fields does not move anything. Do not change trapCount.
After editing a decompiled .src.data, rebuild the script with the same tool; when only field values change the script size does not change, so the EBP section table stays valid (see container-ebp).
gaps: Only the first 26 of the sheet's 1966 chest rows were readable through the Drive connector (summary view; the export endpoint is not available). The unused01 = 0, flags bit 7 = 0 and gilDiamond = gil observations rest on those rows.
Meaning of flags bits 0-5 (multiples of 5 that rise with the chest index, with exceptions) and bit 7.
Base of the sheet's Offset column (0x00 for the first chest of alc_a01 and ald_a02, 0x40 for ald_a01, 0x240 for bds_a01); presumably the offset in <map>.src.data, not confirmed.
How setuptreasure is given the table (argument encoding in the script bytecode) and whether a count precedes it; an editor currently needs the sheet offsets or a pattern scan to find the table.
Coordinate units and axes (whether sheet "Y" is the world Z axis).
Whether uniqueSpawnId N equals "Chest Number" N of the Non-Repeatable Chests sheet or N-1, the highest number used (161 seen; the sheet runs to row 280) and the size of the unique-chest flag array.
Exact randomize-gil formula and whether gilDiamond is ever different from gil in vanilla.
Whether 65535 (none) is accepted in the item fields.
VBF folder of the field EBP files (not recorded in our sources; search the archive for the <map>.ebp names in the sheet).

Traps: why the first trap of srb_b04 starts at 0x3AC instead of 0x3A8 (an extra word after the offset table?), the meaning of +0x05 and +0x0A, the signedness of the positions, and whether uniqueFlagIndex uses the same flag array as chests (said to be likely, not tested, msg 171).
